c: If you want users to select one option from a list of options, you can use a set of radio buttons.
Here is an example of two radio buttons:

description.text:
<input type="radio" id="yes" name="first-time">
<label for="yes">Yes</label>
<input type="radio" id="no" name="first-time">
<label for="no">No</label>

c: In this example, the radio buttons are grouped together by using the same
attribute value. This means that only one radio button can be selected at a time.

c: When you want a user to select multiple options from a list, you can use checkboxes.
Here is an example of checkboxes for food options:

description.text:
<fieldset>
  <legend>Food Options</legend>
  <input type="checkbox" id="pizza" name="food" value="pizza">
  <label for="pizza">Pizza</label>
  <input type="checkbox" id="burger" name="food" value="burger">
  <label for="burger">Burger</label>
</fieldset>
